Subject: Observability export & SIEM routing for private VPC deployment

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

We're preparing the private VPC rollout and need to lock down how telemetry (logs + metrics + traces) will be exported into our Splunk SIEM and the audit evidence we'll retain for SOC2. Key asks up front:

- Can Redwood run a collector inside our VPC (customer-managed) that forwards to Splunk HEC with mTLS?
- What transport modes do you support from the forwarder (HEC over HTTPS, syslog TLS, raw TCP)? Preferred for us is HEC over 443.
- What auth/evidence do you provide for token/key rotation, certs, and KMS integration?
- Retention/egress: we need to know if any telemetry leaves our VPC unencrypted, and what metadata is persisted in Redwood control plane.

I've attached our SIEM requirements spreadsheet for reference (Aether_SIEM_requirements.xlsx). Can you confirm the minimal network ACLs and an expected runbook for acceptance testing?

Proposed timeline: 2 weeks for design + 1 week for validation. We may need a short in-person or video review with Splunk on the token exchange.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Aether Health

Subject: Re: Observability export & SIEM routing for private VPC deployment

Daniel — thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear asks. High-level answer: yes, we support a customer-managed collector deployed in the VPC that forwards to external SIEMs via HEC over TLS; we can also do syslog/TCP where customers require it.

I've sketched a practical acceptance checklist below (we'll formalize into a runbook PDF and share a link):

1) Collector placement: customer-managed EC2/VM in private subnet, or container on customer infra.
2) Outbound: HTTPS to Splunk HEC endpoint (443) using mTLS or HEC token.
3) Buffering & backpressure: local disk buffer + configurable batch size + retry with exponential backoff.
4) Redaction & PII rules: can apply configurable processors inside collector prior to egress.
5) Audit evidence: sha256 checksums of exported bundles + signed delivery receipts in control plane (we'll generate an evidence packet).
6) Cert rotation: recommend 90d client cert rotation; we support automated rotation via our cert-rotation agent if you want Redwood to help.

Action items I propose:
- Marissa: lead the runbook creation and supply our redwood_obsv_runbook_v1.pdf (attached).
- Hiro: follow up on KMS / encryption details and what metadata we store in the control plane.
- Kimberly: confirm any compliance gating items we should pre-populate in the runbook.

I'll loop in Splunk for the HEC specifics in the next message.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_obsv_runbook_v1.pdf (document, 210KB)

Subject: Re: Observability export & SIEM routing for private VPC deployment

Hi Markus / Daniel,

Thanks for the ping. For HEC + token exchange the typical flow is:

- Provision a dedicated HEC input on Splunk Cloud (we will provide a per-environment HEC endpoint).
- Use HEC tokens for ingestion; if you prefer mTLS we can accept client certs but that requires IP allowlisting on our side or a peered private link.
- HEC expects JSON events; compression (gzip) and batching are supported and recommended.
- If you need guaranteed delivery semantics, enable our acknowledgement mode and send compressed batches <= 5MB.

I'll attach the Splunk HEC quickstart and a short checklist for what we need from networking/security.

Link: https://docs.splunk.com/HEC-setup

Regards,
Karla Mendes
Onboarding Engineer — Splunk Cloud
Splunk Onboarding Team

On Fri, Jun 18, 2027 at 4:12 PM Daniel Park <daniel.park@aetherhealth.com> wrote:
> We're preparing the private VPC rollout and need to lock down how telemetry (logs + metrics + traces) will be exported into our Splunk SIEM and the audit evidence we'll retain for SOC2.

Thanks for the clear ask. A few compliance-specific items we need to lock before design sign-off:

- KMS: if you require customer-managed keys for any telemetry at-rest in the forwarder, confirm the KMS provider and key ARN. Redwood supports using your KMS to encrypt the local buffer.
- Evidence: we will produce an 'evidence packet' that includes delivery receipts, checksums, and the runbook version. Need to confirm retention window for evidence (default 90 days unless you ask otherwise).
- Data classification & redaction: provide a sample of 10 representative events so we can show how PII redaction will behave.
- Network: allow outbound 443 to your Splunk HEC host + DNS resolution. If Splunk requires IP allowlisting we will provide the Egress NAT IP(s).
- Client certs: if using mTLS we need a certificate profile (RFC5280) and expected rotation cadence.

If Aether security agrees we can move this to a 30–45 minute design call and finalize the acceptance test plan.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
